details:
I would like for VRChat to consider the potential of using Avatar Impostors to help assist with the problem of using Very Poor avatars at a larger scale.

I believe that Very Poor should be an available option within the Performance Rank Blocking menu, and that it can be moderated with the use of Avatar Impostors and sometimes the fallback system.

You should be able to set a limit or radius to drastically reduce the amount of Very Poor avatars on screen, and if they are currently not “shown” due to those settings, they should fall back to their Impostor (or Fallback if available), and if they are *too* far (blocked by the original nearby avatar rendering system) then they should default to the Impostor or default triangle models.

Very Poor avatars *can* result in large or unnecessary performance consumption, but this can be vastly reduced if the avatars can be managed such that only a few of them are ever *completely* on the screen at any given point in time.
title: [Feature Request] Rework “Very Poor” Avatar Blocking

Having to go to the website for advanced features like this while everything else is accessible inside the sdk control panel is just annoying)

Bumping this, as it's been over a year and imposters are now non-experimental and are on track to replace fallbacks since mid-2025.

Having at least some sort of preview in Unity for impostors before uploading would be very useful.

I've witnessed multiple people's avatar imposters be unintentionally generated with the clothing toggled off, due to the way that some clothing toggles are set up.

And it can be frustrating for users debugging and adjusting imposters due to the 10 impostors generation per day limit on the VRChat website.

Being able to generate imposters on your own hardware (provided, if your hardware is capable / strong enough to generate imposters, I'm not sure what the requirements for this would be) would help streamline the current imposter fine-tuning process significantly.

Currently, seeing the results of changes made to the VRCImpostorSettings and the VRCImposterEnvironment on a VRChat avatar means:

1 - Signing into the VRChat SDK in Unity

2 - Re-uploading the avatar again with the new or adjusted VRCImpostorSettings and VRCImposterEnvironment components.

3 - Logging into the VRChat website after the new upload is finished.

4 - Deleting the old imposters on the VRChat website.

5 - Generating new imposters.

6 - Waiting for the generation to finish (this can take as little as a few minutes or longer depending on the avatar's complexity).

7 - Once it's done generating, opening VRChat on desktop / in VR / on your phone or tablet to preview the generated imposter in your menu.

8 - Repeating this whole process over again if you don't like how the imposter turned out, until having to wait until the next day if you manage to generate 10 imposters in one day.

Currently, there's no way to preview generated imposters directly on the VRChat website or in Unity, so viewing them in VRChat in-game is the only way to preview them.

Providing a button to push inside Unity to generate the imposters, like others have said, would reduce the amount of friction involved in generating imposters, which currently involves remembering to go login to the VRChat website directly after uploading an avatar.

Also, providing a way to actually wear the imposter in-game, even if it's only local and not visible to remote players, would make it a lot easier to know if there's something wrong with your imposter when it moves as well: https://feedback.vrchat.com/impostors/p/provide-the-way-to-wear-impostor-avatar-itself

This would be similar to how you can preview your Fallback Shaders in VRChat, and should be added to the action menu next to "Fallback Shaders" + in settings as well. (See screenshot of VRChat action menu attached).

Adding a way to wear the imposter in-game reduces the reliance on having to have someone else in an instance with you take screenshots or record a video or relying a second account to see how the imposter actually looks in motion.

VRCImposterEnvironment is also still not documented in the creator-docs: https://feedback.vrchat.com/impostors/p/documentation-for-the-vrc-impostor-environment-component-is-missing | https://creators.vrchat.com/avatars/avatar-impostors with no mention of how 'Sky Color', 'Equator Color', and 'Ground Color' impact the imposter generation result. (see screenshot).

Additionally, the current documentation for "Transforms To Ignore" doesn't specify if the component includes child items or if it will it ignore all child items or not. It just reads "Ignores these transforms when capturing data for the impostor. This will hide them from the final result. This is independent of the bone that VRCImpostorSettings is placed on." 

Someone asked about this in the VRChat discord to the chatbot a few months ago and the chatbot said this in response: 

"There is no mention of recursive behavior (children being automatically ignored) in the provided sources. Because of that, I can't reliably say whether children are also excluded or if you must list each transform you want ignored."

With imposters set to fully replace fallback avatars in the near future, improvements to the avatar imposter generation experience and documentation would be very appreciated and would reduce confusion around imposter generation settings going forward :3! 

Thank you for reading!

Remember to click the upvote button at top of this page, to the left of the "SDK Client Side Imposter Preview" title of this post if you want to show your support for generating imposters through the SDK on your own hardware!

Commenting under the main original post as well will also help show support for this feature if you want this :3!

Even a simple "Bump!" or "Agreed!" comment helps push this and other feedback requests like it onto VRChat's radar and potentially their future roadmap / get a feedback request marked as 'Tracked' or at least 'Interested'.

Be sure to upvote and comment the other feedback posts linked in this post if you are interested in seeing those be implemented / updated as well!

In my case there are a few specific reasons:

1. I often don't update my avatar, I just upload it as a separate version, because when I mess something up, I always know that I can use different avatars, there are also people who don't create master avatars, only a few specific variants with a few clothes, if creating an impostor will be took as much time in the future as it does now, creating a dozen or so impostors will simply be terribly time-consuming to generate for each separate version.

2. After a wave of problems with avatar rippers, of which I was a victim, I know that rippers are still able to extract avatars straight from the vrchat cache, and this causes me to use an avatar protected with DexProtect so that the situation that affected me would not occur. it never happened again, unfortunately, it will not be possible to create an impostor from such a secured avatar, which means that this function is still useless for me, and I must admit that I previously tried to create my avatar in the Quest version, but with poor results, because the requirements for the quest are too restrictive, and the level of advancement of my avatar is simply beyond the ability to create one that looks good and has any good performance to be visible to others.

3. I think that not everyone wants to be visible to others in the same way, but simply to be visible differently than a robot, but they also like to change avatars often, including public ones, which makes the use of impostors also useless, because we are not able to able to generate impostors for public avatars, and even if the author of a given avatar had such an opportunity, imagine how many avatars would have to undergo such a transformation, where in fact many authors, after completing a public avatar, usually do not return to it.

I think these are three strong arguments for simply adding the option of choosing an impostor yourself, instead of generating it for each specific avatar separately, because I must admit that I really like your new idea, it finally solves the problem of the lack of Quest avatars, but it requires slight refinement so that everyone is satisfied.

details: As you can see nowadays, with most games unable to prevent their models from being ripped by ripper, we seem to be helpless. However, I have thought about why we don’t have a system similar to the shield feature that currently allows you to unlock avatars of players who own fixed ranks in VRChat. It would be fantastic if those without permission can only see the fallback avatar. This would be very convenient as we would no longer have to fear ripper stealing our private avatars. Of course, we could also control and filter friends to make it harder for imposters to steal avatars. Many of us no longer feel safe in public instances and would feel more comfortable if this feature were considered and implemented. The root of the issue is that ripper can easily load your avatar, so let's create a feature to filter them out. If this is approved, there will certainly be many who disagree, but ultimately, this is a way to protect the community’s interests.
title: This feature allows you to filter and see your private avatar for other players.

details:
Currently, accessing the Imposter preview requires 3 clicks from the avatar change screen.  

Because of this, many users never notice the preview feature exists. As a result, even if an inappropriate (NSFW) Imposter is generated, people often use it without realizing it.

If a small Imposter preview was displayed directly on the avatar change screen (like in the attached image), even beginners would immediately notice if their Imposter is nude or inappropriate and could seek help before using it.

アバター変更画面でインポスタープレビューを直接表示してください

現在、インポスタープレビューにアクセスするには、アバター変更画面から3回クリックする必要があります。

そのため、多くのユーザーはプレビュー機能の存在に気づきません。結果として、不適切な（NSFW）インポスターが生成された場合でも、気づかないうちに使用してしまうことがよくあります。

添付画像のように、アバター変更画面に小さなインポスタープレビューが直接表示されれば、初心者でもインポスターが裸や不適切なものであることにすぐに気づき、サポートを求めることができます。
title: Please show Imposter previews directly on the Avatar Change screen

details:
Many players unknowingly use “Imposters unsuitable for public spaces” because they don’t check the preview.

Every time I see this, I face a dilemma:  

Should I directly tell the person how to delete the Imposter? Or should I stay silent so I don’t embarrass them?  

(It’s the same feeling as wondering whether you should tell someone their fly is open.)

If there was a system to discreetly report the issue without the user noticing, this problem would be solved. After the report, the Imposter could be removed or regenerated either by moderator review or an automatic process.

プレイヤーがゲーム内から不適切なインポスターを通報できるようにしてください。

多くのプレイヤーはプレビューを確認せずに「公共の場にふさわしくないインポスター」を無意識のうちに使用しています。

このような状況に遭遇するたびに、私はジレンマに直面します。

インポスターの削除方法を直接本人に伝えるべきか？それとも、相手を困らせないように黙っているべきか？

（まるで、誰かのズボンのチャックが開いていることを指摘すべきかどうか迷うのと同じような感覚です。）

ユーザーに気づかれずに問題を通報できるシステムがあれば、この問題は解決するでしょう。通報後、インポスターはモデレーターによる審査、または自動処理によって削除または再生成されます。
title: Please allow players to report inappropriate Imposters from within the game

details:
The Imposter generation feature on the VRChat website is currently not functioning. The process starts but consistently ends with an error message.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Go to https://vrchat.com/home/avatars and open the details page of an avatar that does not have an Imposter.

2.Click the "Generate Imposters" button at the bottom of the page.

3. The button text changes to "Generating Imposters" as expected.

4. After a few seconds, a system message appears: "System Message - Oh no! We tried, but we could not generate an impostor version of the avatar [Avatar Name]."

5. Even after waiting, no Imposter is generated.

Additional Context:

・I successfully generated an Imposter on April 4th without any issues, suggesting this is a recent regression.

・Similar issues have been reported by another user on X (formerly Twitter).
title: Imposter generation fails on VRChat website with "Oh no!" system message
